brief: The allotments have 17 plots, a lattice, a glasshouse, 38 pieces of furniture, a two-crop majority read (#159) and a harvest cycle — and almost nobody in them. #154 counted the WHOLE hand-act population at 28 acts a year across SIX worlds, 11 of them sow rungs: about five acts per seed-year, so anything a hand does to a plot is capped at five. #159 then built inter-cropping on top of that cap and its own probe measured the result at 264 samples in 139,000 (0.19%) — its Law says it outright: the SUPPLY was always the cap. RE-COUNT THE 28 ON HEAD FIRST; it is dated #154 and #159 has landed since. Then raise the SUPPLY — `allotRate` / `spawnAllotAgent`, the arrival rate and the window — never the share, and measure presence per PLOT rather than choices. Carry c257 with it, because it is the same domain and three lines: `cartToday()` and `drayToday()` are `hash(day,k)` UNSALTED, so the allotment cart's calendar is identical in every world; `WIND_SALT` exists for exactly this. Cross street x Scale/World is an EMPTY cell — 0 entries in 169 iterations.
successLooksLike: Over a growing season a plot is worked several times, not once: hand-acts per seed-year go from ~5 into double figures with the plot lattice and the crop invariants untouched (tomato outside the span 0; tender at stage 3 in deep winter at HEAD's 30), and the cart's days differ between two seeds where today they are identical.
avoid: Do not widen INTER_SHARE or any other share — #159 swept it and 0.70 and 1.00 came back byte-identical. Do not add a plot or a species. Do not change the plot's footprint: a plot OWNS x [ox,ox+4) y [oy,oy+3) and never its WEST side, which is where sendToPlot lands.
